title: Control Plane Performance Evidence

architecture_components.role: Client-facing HTTP, JSON, route metrics, SSE entrypoints, and v3 thread history refreshes.
Assignment polling, long-poll waiters, DynamoDB operation vocabulary, and store actor command flow.
Provider progress normalization, line retention, client event fanout, and task stream projection.
Timer, waiter-map, approval wait, and actor shutdown paths that can become idle CPU or goroutine pressure.
HTTP and store metric aggregation that must stay bounded while feeding OTel/X-Ray/CloudWatch evidence.

hot_paths.risk: high route volume can contend on transaction metric aggregation
hot_paths.candidate: keep route-pattern cardinality bounded and watch allocation/lock cost

hot_paths.risk: poll, lease, and append metrics run on assignment/store hot paths
hot_paths.candidate: keep store metric aggregation bounded and compare operation-level cost before optimizing

hot_paths.risk: task screens with many historical threads can over-copy progress lines while computing active SSE filters
hot_paths.candidate: prefer active stream target projection over full visible thread copies for subscription paths

hot_paths.risk: fine-grained provider progress can create many render/normalize calls
hot_paths.candidate: batch provider progress before rendering and preserve structured fallback behavior

hot_paths.risk: polling and long-poll waiters can create goroutine pressure or stale busy state
hot_paths.candidate: keep long-poll waiters off the actor critical path and watch waiter/goroutine count

hot_paths.risk: workspace SSE subscribers can amplify each progress event into visibility checks and non-blocking channel sends
hot_paths.candidate: measure subscriber fanout in local pressure before expanding live event payloads

hot_paths.risk: tool approval long-poll waiters can add timer and waiter-map pressure when provider tools request human decisions
hot_paths.candidate: keep approval waits bounded and watch goroutine/timer deltas under stalled approvals

assertions: endpoint/API contracts must not change for performance evidence work
lightweight benchmark evidence must run without live credentials
race/concurrency evidence must be emitted as a workflow artifact before high-traffic fixes are accepted
local pressure evidence must include httptest coverage for the v3 thread history endpoint hot path
local pressure evidence must emit measured allocation, latency, CPU, goroutine, subscriber-fanout findings, and per-scenario capacity estimates
local pressure evidence must emit stable closed-loop candidate artifacts for measured pressure scenarios
manual local pressure pprof must emit CPU, heap, and goroutine profile file metadata without changing endpoint contracts
local pressure findings must carry closed-loop candidate required artifacts and executable adoption commands
live load evidence must stay redacted and use aiagentload rather than ad-hoc curl loops
live load evidence must emit requests_per_second, success_per_second, failure_rate_pct, endpoint findings, capacity_estimate, and load_generator_resource_delta
live load evidence may attach opt-in pprof sample metadata but must never persist pprof profile bodies
pprof collection must use loopback-only RIIDO_AI_SERVER_PPROF_ADDR
performance candidates must name the hot path, risk, existing evidence, and next verifier candidate

performance evidence must expose a generated file_architecture_index that maps hot-path files to architecture components, pressure dimensions, OTel/X-Ray/CloudWatch signal names, evidence refs, hot path ids, and executable target verifier commands

architecture query evidence must let agents map a known changed file to pressure dimensions, observability signals, optimization candidates, and target verifier commands without rereading the generated architecture prose

loop.observation: Control-plane already has isolated load, metrics, and benchmark evidence, but high-traffic risk candidates, local CPU/resource deltas, and opt-in pprof sample metadata are not emitted from one executable performance loop.
loop.hypothesis: A performance evidence sidecar can bind endpoint, DB/store, SSE, scheduling, progress, local pressure, pprof, and load surfaces into one generated audit and lightweight benchmark workflow without changing external contracts or persisting profile bodies.
loop.execute: Verify hot-path files and benchmark/test functions, publish lightweight benchmark output, publish lightweight race/concurrency output, publish local pressure throughput/latency/allocation/CPU/goroutine/subscriber-fanout evidence with measured findings and capacity estimates, expose local pressure pprof metadata, export pressure scenario candidates as a closed-loop candidate artifact, expose loopback pprof and live-load commands, make aiagentload emit throughput/failure/capacity/resource findings plus opt-in pprof sample metadata, and generate candidate optimization rows whose findings carry closed-loop adoption commands.
loop.evaluate: The verifier fails on missing benchmark coverage, missing race artifact wiring, missing local pressure evidence, missing capacity estimates, missing local pressure candidate artifact, missing local pprof command/profile metadata path, missing finding-level closed-loop candidate adoption paths, missing pprof loopback contract, missing aiagentload live command, stale generated docs, non-strict workflow artifacts, architecture queries that omit match_kind, component summaries, direct/fallback hit counts, or aiagentload tests that lose throughput/capacity/resource/pprof fields.
loop.retrospective: This keeps performance work in an open loop first: measure resource pressure and rank hot paths before promoting repeated bottlenecks into closed-loop gates.
